description: The line plot illustrates the performance of two evaluation methods—Direct Assessment (green line) and Pairwise Ranking (blue line)—as the merging ratio between evaluator language models trained on different formats is varied, with a third line (black) representing average performance across both metrics. The x-axis, labeled “(Direct Assessment : Pairwise Ranking) Merging Ratio,” spans from 1:9 to 9:1 in increments of 0.9, indicating the proportional weighting of the two training formats. The left y-axis, labeled “Direct Assessment Pearson Correlation,” ranges from 0.500 to 0.675 in steps of 0.025 and measures the correlation for the Direct Assessment method; the green line begins at approximately 0.495 at 1:9, rises steeply to a peak of 0.670 at 5.5:4.5, then declines gradually to 0.595 at 9:1. The right y-axis, labeled “Pairwise Ranking Agreement Accuracy,” ranges from 50 to 80 in steps of 5 and measures the accuracy for the Pairwise Ranking method; the blue line starts near 75 at 1:9, peaks slightly above 77 at 3.7:6.3, then drops sharply to 50 at 9:1. The black line, representing average performance, begins at 0.578 (left axis), rises to a peak of 0.625 at 5.5:4.5, then declines to 0.525 at 9:1. The plot visually supports the caption’s claim that Direct Assessment (green) is more sensitive to changes in the merging ratio than Pairwise Ranking (blue), especially as the ratio shifts toward higher Direct Assessment weighting, where Pairwise Ranking performance deteriorates more rapidly.
